title: Cancer: current or history, and metastases
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cancer as documented at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint
Bone pain and follow-up for history of colon cancer.

HPI
Pt is a 70 y/o male presenting for f/u of history of colon cancer. Primary malignancy was surgically removed and treated several years ago. Pt states he feels generally well otherwise but reports dull, aching pain in the lumbar spine and pelvis over the last 3 months. Pain is constant, rated 4/10, and slightly worse at night. He denies any new bowel changes, weight loss, or fever. He reports that his primary site remains clear.

Review of Systems
Constitutional: No fever, chills, or night sweats. No weight loss.
MSK: Positive for low-grade back pain. No joint swelling.
GI: No diarrhea, constipation, or hematochezia.
Neuro: No numbness or weakness in lower extremities.

Social History
Retired. Lives with wife. Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol use.

Family History
Father: Colorectal cancer. Mother: Hypertension.

Medication List
Acetaminophen 650mg BID PRN for pain.
Lisinopril 10mg daily.
Atorvastatin 20mg daily.

Vitals
BP: 132/82
HR: 74 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 98% on RA
Wt: 195 lbs

Recent Labs
Hb: 13.2 g/dL
WBC: 7.5 K/uL
Plt: 210 K/uL
eGFR: 72 mL/min

Exam
General: Alert, oriented x3, in no acute distress.
Respiratory: CTAB.
Cardiovascular: RRR, no murmurs.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, non-distended.
Musculoskeletal: Tenderness noted over L4-L5 and S1. No focal neurological deficits.

Assessment
1. Colon cancer: Primary site shows no evidence of local recurrence. Treatment of primary site is complete.
2. Bone metastasis: Pt presents with symptoms of metastases to bone.

Plan
1. Pain management: Continue Acetaminophen as needed. Consider escalating to a scheduled analgesic if pain persists.
2. Imaging: Order X-ray of lumbar spine and pelvis to evaluate bone metastasis.
3. F/u: Return to clinic in 4 weeks to review imaging and adjust pain management plan.

Electronically signed, L. Moreau, DO, 05/14/2026
explanations: The colon cancer was excised or eradicated, no treatment is directed to it and there is no evidence of it: personal history Z85.038 (no HCC). Any metastasis is still coded as a current secondary malignancy.
Bone metastases: C79.51, secondary malignant neoplasm of bone (HCC 18, which outranks the primary-site HCC).

distractors.why: Treatment ended and there is no evidence of the primary: code personal history (Z85), not active cancer.
Metastasis is coded as a secondary malignancy, even when the primary is history.
The metastases are in bone, not the liver.

hccs.label: Cancer Metastatic to Bone/Other and Unspecified Metastatic Cancer; Acute Leukemia Except Myeloid
